title: Atomically precise triple-step staircase on a vicinal silicon surface: Is it Si(5 5 7), Si(7 7 10) or Si(8 8 11)?
authors: A. N. Chaika, A. Yu. Aladyshkin, V. N. Semenov, A. S. Aladyshkina, A. M. Ionov, S. I. Bozhko
abstract: Scanning tunneling microscopy studies of periodic arrays of triple steps fabricated on single-crystalline Si(5 5 7) wafers demonstrate several possible atomic structures of consecutive steps and Si(1 1 1) terraces maintaining the same periodicity on micrometer-sized surface areas. Detailed analysis of the atomically resolved data reveals the formation of Si(8 8 11) triple-step staircase with a period of 18b=5.99 nm in projection onto the terrace plane, where b=0.333 nm is the distance between atomic rows for the Si(1 1 1)1x1 surface. Schematic models for several possible configurations of either 7x7 or 5x5-reconstructed terraces and triple steps are proposed.
summary: This work uses advanced Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) to determine the exact atomic structure of a triple-step staircase on vicinal silicon wafers. By analyzing periodicity and cross-sectional profiles, the authors argue that the observed structure corresponds specifically to the $	ext{Si}(8\ 8\ 11)$ orientation. This provides an atomically precise understanding of surface reconstruction relevant for materials science applications.
main_problem: The study aims to definitively determine the correct atomic structure of a triple-step staircase formed on vicinal silicon surfaces, distinguishing between proposed candidates like Si(5 5 7), Si(7 7 10), or Si(8 8 11).
main_result: Analysis of STM data strongly suggests that the observed periodicity corresponds to an $	ext{Si}(8\ 8\ 11)$ orientation, yielding a period of $L = 18b \approx 5.99$ nm.
method: The research relies heavily on Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) measurements, utilizing differential D(x,y) maps and cross-section analysis to resolve atomic arrangements.
model_or_system: The physical system is vicinal silicon wafers ($	ext{Si}(h\ h\ m)$), which exhibit arrays of $	ext{Si}(1\ 1\ 1)$ terraces separated by mono- or multiatomic steps forming a periodic staircase structure. The analysis compares experimental data to theoretical models based on $7	imes 7$ reconstructions.
key_observables: Periodicity ($L$) of the staircase, atomic structure of steps and mini-terraces, and characteristic distances like $b=0.333$ nm.
important_parameters: The measured periodicity is found to be $L = 18b \approx 5.99$ nm; miscut angles are also discussed in relation to the proposed structures.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that observed features can be mapped onto ideal atomic lattice models, though limitations regarding step edge reconstructions and defects are noted.
figures_summary: Figures show D(x,y) maps and cross-sections confirming periodicities ($L=18b$) and illustrating the sequence of monatomic steps separated by $7	imes 7$ reconstructed mini-terraces consistent with $	ext{Si}(8\ 8\ 11)$.
paper_structure: The paper methodically analyzes STM data, comparing measured periodicities against theoretical predictions for different crystal orientations ($	ext{Si}(5\ 5\ 7)$, etc.), ultimately converging on the periodicity and structure associated with $	ext{Si}(8\ 8\ 11)$.
why_interesting: While focused on materials science, the precise atomic characterization of surfaces using STM techniques is foundational to understanding interfaces, which are critical in quantum device engineering (e.g., superconducting qubits or quantum dots).

figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic models of the periodic Si(5 5 7) (a) and Si(7 7 10) (b) triple-step staircases with a (112)- oriented triple step (a) and a sequence of monatomic step, Si(1 1 1) mini-terrace and (001)-oriented double step with height equal to two distances 2d between neighboring silicon atomic layers (b) [1, 16]. The model presentations do not show adatoms on the 7×7-reconstructed Si(111) terraces and reconstructions at the step edges. The step periodicity in projection onto the terrace plane and along the vicinal surface are indicated as L and L*, respectively.

Figure 2. Typical differential D(x,y) map obtained from a large-area STM image of a regular triple-step array fabricated on the Si(5 5 7) wafer (top panel, image size of 640 × 210 nm2, tunneling voltage U = -1.8 V, tunneling current I = 40 pA, scale bar corresponds to 100 nm). The solid line at the bottom shows the profile of the D(x,y) map averaged along the vertical direction and illustrates the regularity of the triple-step array on length scales exceeding 500 nm.

Figure 3. LEED pattern taken at an incident electron beam energy of 75 eV from the triple-step staircase fabricated on the Si(5 5 7) wafer. The marked horizontal rows correspond to the 7×7 reconstruction on the Si(1 1 1) terraces. The periodic spots in horizontal rows correspond to the formation of the regular triple-step array on large surface areas..

Figure 4. (a) STM topography image after global plane correction (image size 48.4 × 30 nm², U = 1.5 V, I = 60 pA) acquired at room temperature reveals a periodic array of triple steps and Si(1 1 1) terraces. Each terrace comprises one complete 7×7 unit cell and an additional row of adatoms. (b) After subtraction of a plane parallel to the terraces, the same image shows all flat (1 1 1) terraces horizontal. The red line shows the height variation of the aligned image as a function of the x-coordinate.
